scenario: Conversation between two friends who have known each other for a long time. One of them used to make fun of the other because English was not their first language.
learner_goal: Apologize sincerely to your friend (<extra_info>Extra information: you used to make fun of your friend's English skills as they were learning the language. Now you regret your actions and want to apologize</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Accept the apology but express the hurt caused by the actions (<extra_info>Extra information: you were hurt by your friend's actions and it affected your confidence</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Sophia James
transcript.content: Miles, I want to apologize — I was wrong to make fun of your English when you were learning. I'm really sorry; I regret hurting you and I take responsibility for that. I want to do better and be someone who supports you, not laughs at you.

transcript.speaker: Miles Hawkins
transcript.content: Thank you, Sophia. I appreciate you saying that. It did hurt — when people laughed at my English I felt embarrassed and it knocked my confidence for a long time. I forgive you, but I want you to know it affected me. Going forward, what helps is encouragement and no jokes about the way I speak. I value our friendship and I’m willing to move forward. Maybe we can talk more about it over coffee at the market sometime.
